UNDER UTILISATION OF ALLOCATED FUNDS AND INCREASING SHORTFALL 
(RECOMMENDATION PARA NO. 1) 
 
1.5  The Committee had observed/recommended: 
The Committee in their 3 rd Report (DFG 2024 -25) at recommendation 
no. 1 have observed that the revised procedure for release of central funds to 
States/UTs was introduced by the Department of Expenditure, MoF w.e.f . 
31stJuly, 2021, and even after three years of its introduction, the desired results 
as envisaged by the Department, have not been achieved. The Committee, 
therefore, recommended that, the Department should make serious efforts and 
proactively liaise with its c ounterparts in the States/UTs and State Fisheries 
Departments to address this issue for positive results.  
Now, the Committee have been informed that to bring more efficiency in 
cash management at both Centre and States levels, an alternative fund flow 
mechanism for releasing central funds has been introduced on “Just -in-Time” 
basis under Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS) namely SNA-SPARSH from 
1st June, 2024, wherein, 28 schemes including Pradhan Mantri Matsya 
Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) have been on boarded. Under the new system, 26 
States have been on boarded, however, the pace of fund flow has been slow 
due to la ck of understanding by the states to adhere to the 
compliances/guidelines of SNA-SPARSH, delay in contributing matching share 

 
3 
 
by the State Governments and non -receipt of physical and financial progress 
(utilization certificates) on time from States/UTs and other stakeholders.  
The Committee are concerned that, the Department is unable to 
completely utilise the allocated budget and the shortfall of the Department has 
been increasing continuously. This underutilization of funds is also affecting the 
implementation and outcomes of the flagship scheme Pradhan Mantri Matsya 
Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) and expenditure under the Scheduled Caste Sub 
Plan (SCSP) and Scheduled Tribes Sub Plan (STSP) which in turn is affecting 
the goals of uplifting the socio -economic conditions and general well-being of 
the poor and traditional fishermen of the country. The Committee, therefore, 
recommend that the Department may explore the possibility of devising an 
incentive scheme for State/UT governments, particularly to those States/UTs 
who promptly comply with t he SNA -SPARSH guidelines, release their state 
matching share in time along with Utilization Certificates and whose 
performance in implementing the schemes of the Department and spending 
under Scheduled Castes Sub Plan (SCSP), Scheduled Tribes Sub Plan (STSP) 
is substantial. The Committee would like to be apprised of the steps taken by 
the Department and progress achieved in this regard. 
1.6 In its Action Taken Reply, the Department has submitted: 
“The observation of the committee has been noted for necessary compliance. 
The Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance vide OM 
No.1(27)/PFMS/2020 dated 13th July 2023 has notified an alternative fund flow 
mechanism for releasing central funds to the State Governments on “ Just-in-
Time” basis under Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS). This new system has 
been named as SNA-SPARSH wherein 28 schemes including PMMSY have 
been on boarded with effect from 1 st June, 2024. Under this new system, 28 
States have been on -boarding on the SNA SPARSH  platform. Lack of 
understanding by the states to adhere to the compliances of SNA -SPARSH, 
transition phase between SNA and SNA -SPARSH made the process slow for 
the States to adopt the new procedure and Non- compliance of the Guidelines 
in time by the Stat es are few of the major point for slow expenditure. The 
Department has been working in close coordination with the States and these 

 
4 
 
issues have been addressed from time to time. As such, better performance in 
the upcoming days is expected.” 
1.7 The Committee, were concerned with the Department ’s inability to 
completely utilize the allocated budget , which in turn affected  the 
implementation and outcomes of the flagship scheme Pradhan Mantri Matsya 
Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) and expenditure under the Scheduled Caste Sub Plan 
(SCSP) and Scheduled Tribes Sub Plan (STSP) . The Committee,  had therefore 
recommended that, the Department may explore the possibility of devising an 
incentive scheme for State/UT governments, particularly for those States/UTs 
which promptly comply with the SNA -SPARSH guidelines and to release their 
state matching share in time along with Utilisation Certifi cates and whose 
performance in implementing the schemes of the Department and spending 
under Scheduled Castes Sub Plan (SCSP), Scheduled Tribes Sub Plan (STSP) is 
substantial. The Department, in their reply, has not provided specific inputs on 
the possibility of devising an incentive scheme, as recommended by the 
Committee, or on its potential role in improving the utilization of the allocated 
budget under SCSP and STSP. The Committee, therefo re, reiterate its 
recommendation and encourage the Department to consider formulating such 
a scheme. 
SCHEDULED CASTES SUB PLAN (SCSP) 
(RECOMMENDATION PARA NO. 4) 
 
1.8 The Committee had observed/recommended: 
The Committee in their 3rd Report (DFG 2024-25) at recommendation no 
5, expressed serious concern at the declining trend of utilization of funds under 
SCSP and recommended the Department to analyze the reasons for non -
receipt of the proposals from the state Governments and initiate suitable action 

 
5 
 
including review of features, terms & conditions, eligibility criteria, etc and 
ensure the receipt of proposals from the state/ UT Governments for optimal 
utilization of the funds under SCSP.  
The Committee has been informed that the Government of India has 
highlighted the matter with the States/UTs having sizeable Schedule Caste 
beneficiaries in all the review meetings and they have been advised to ensure 
Mandatory earmarking of minimum 16.6% o f the budget of PMSSY for the 
benefits of scheduled caste beneficiaries. Further, States/UTs are advised to 
include SC/ST beneficiaries accordingly in their annual action plans and End 
Implementing Agencies i.e. Central Government entities including the National 
Fisheries Development Board (NFDB) to include suitable interventions/  
activities for supporting SC population appropriately in their respective Annual 
Action Plan or Project Proposals.  
The Committee, appreciate the efforts taken by the Department to 
ensure and encourage States/UTs to submit proposals under SCSP component 
of PMMSY, however, the Committee, observe that the actual expenditure of 
funds under SCSP component of PMMSY from the financial years 2022-23 to 
2024-25 have been continuously decreasing. The Committee infers that 
decreasing actual expenditure of funds allocated for SCSP would mean that the 
efforts taken by the Department are not materializing in increasing actual 
expenditure under SCSP. The Committee, therefore recommend that the 
Department continue with their efforts so as to ensure maximum participation 
of Scheduled Castes population in the schemes implemented by the 
Department and reiterate their earlier recommendation  that the Department 
may devise a mechanism to incentivize /encourage States/UTs to send 
proposals under the SCSP so that the intended benefits of the scheme come 
to fruition. 
1.9 In its Action Taken Reply, the Department has submitted: 
“The Department of Fisheries, Government of India, has consistently 
highlighted the matter in all review meetings with States/UTs having a sizeable 
Scheduled Caste beneficiary population. The States/UTs also been advised to 
ensure that minimum 16.6% of the  Schedule Caste beneficiaries are included 

 
6 
 
for financial assistance in PMMSY project proposals while preparing the state 
annual action plan. Further, the measures taken up by the Department of 
Fisheries, Government of India in this regard include: (i) Mandatory earmarking 
of minimum 16.6% of the bu dget allocated under Schedule Cast Sub -Plan 
(SCSP) for the benefits of scheduled caste beneficiaries and advising 
States/UTs to include SC/ST beneficiaries accordingly in their annual action 
plans. Specific mention has been made in the annual administrativ e approval 
of the Scheme, in accordance with the Ministry of Finance's instructions, that 
the funds earmarked for Scheduled Caste beneficiaries are to be utilized 
exclusively for their development (ii) Requesting the End Implementing 
Agencies i.e. Central Government entities including the National Fisheries 
Development Board (NFDB) to include suitable interventions/activities for 
supporting SC population appropriately in their respective Annual Action Plan 
or Project Proposals. Similarly, State Governments and Union Territories are 
regularly requested to make specific allocations for Scheduled Castes in their 
Annual Action Plans, self -contained proposals, and Detailed Project Reports 
(DPRs), based on the percentage of the SC population within their jurisdiction.” 
 
1.10 The Committee were concerned about the decreasing actual expenditure 
of funds under SCSP component of PMMSY from the financial years 2022-23 to 
2024-25 and further inferred that the efforts taken by the Department are not 
materializing in increasing actual  expenditure under SCSP. The Committee, 
therefore had recommended that the Department may analyze the reasons for 
non-receipt of the proposals from the state Governments and initiate suitable 
action including review of features, terms & conditions, el igibility criteria, etc . 
and ensure the receipt of proposals from the state/ UT Governments . The 
Department, however, has not answered on this specific recommendation of the 
Committee. The Committee, therefore, reiterate their recommendation that the 
Department may explore the possibility of reviewing the features, terms and 

 
7 
 
conditions and eligibility criteria etc. under SCSP  to ensure maximum 
participation and optimal utilization of funds under SCSP .    
 
DEVELOPMENT OF CLIMATE RESILIENT FISHERMEN VILLAGES AROUND 
RIVERS 
(RECOMMENDATION PARA NO. 6) 
 
1.11 The Committee had observed/recommended: 
 The Committee has been informed that the Department of Fisheries, 
under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), has identified 
100 coastal fishermen villages situated close to the coastline as Climate 
Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages (CRCFV) to enhance the economic 
resilience of communities impacted by climate change along with development 
of climate -resilient fisheries through initiatives such as seaweed cultivation, 
ornamental fisheries, artificial reefs, sea ranching and promotion of green fuel 
for fishing etc. Further, safety and security measures for fishermen and fishing 
vessels, insurance programmes, livelihood and nutritional support, Kisan Credit 
Cards, training and capacity building are also focused upon. Provision of need-
based facil ities, including common facilities like fish drying yards, fish 
processing centers, fish markets, fishing jetties, ice plants, cold storages and 
emergency rescue facilities are also incorporated.  
The Committee note that the country has a vast potential in Inland fisheries 
comprising of 0.28 million km of rivers and canals, 1.2 million ha flood plain 
lakes, 2.45 million ha of ponds and tanks and 3.15 million ha of reservoirs, 
which contributes aroun d 13.9 MMT to total fish production. Most of the 
traditional fishing communities who lack socio-economic stability reside around 
these vast rivers and lakes. The Committee therefore recommend that the 
Department should devise a scheme for these traditional  fishermen 
communities who reside alongside rivers and explore the possibility of 
development of their villages into climate resilient fishermen villages in 
consultation with States/UTs. The committee would like to be apprised of the 
measures taken by the Department in this regard. 

 
8 
 
1.12 In its Action Taken Reply, the Department has submitted: 
“The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) inter-alia 
provides support to the Coastal States/UTs for development of Integrated 
Modern Coastal Fishing Villages.  Under PMMSY, the proposals with total 
outlay of Rs.7756.46 lakh for development of total 11 integrated modern coastal 
villages have been approved which include (i) nine coastal villages at a cost of 
Rs. 6106.61 lakh in Kerala, (ii) one Coastal village at a cost of Rs.899.85 lakh 
in Lakshadweep and (iii) one coastal village at a cost of Rs. 75 0 lakh in West 
Bengal. In addition, under the PMMSY, the Department of Fisheries, 
Government of India, in consultation with the coastal States/UTs has also 
identified 100 coastal fishermen villages situated close to the coastline for 
development as Climate  Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages (CRCFV) to 
make them economically vibrant fishermen villages. The National Fisheries 
Development Board (NFDB), Hyderabad has been made a nodal agency and 
the proposal for development of the identified 100 coastal villa ges at a total 
cost of Rs. 200 crore has been approved under the PMMSY. As per PMMSY 
scheme guidelines, both the components i.e. Integrated Modern Coastal 
Fishing Villages and Climate Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages are 
implemented in coastal States a nd Union Territories only, hence, no projects 
have been sanctioned under these components to inland States. The PMMSY 
scheme has completed its schematic tenure on 31.03.2025 and one year no 
cost extension has been approved by the Government. The scheme is currently 
under evaluation. Based on the outcomes of this evaluation, the proposal for 
the inclusion of Climate -Resilient Fishermen Villages around rivers will be 
examined and considered for inclusion in the subsequent scheme.” 
 
1.13 The Committee had recommended that the Department of Fisheries 
should devise a scheme for traditional fishermen communities who reside 
alongside rivers and explore the possibility of development of their villages into 
climate resilient fishermen villages i n consultation with States/UTs. The 
Department in their reply have stated that PMMSY scheme has completed its 

 
9 
 
schematic tenure on 31.03.2025 and thereafter, one year no cost extension has 
been approved by the Government, however, the scheme is currently under 
evaluation and based on the outcomes of this evaluation, the proposal of the 
Committee for the inclusion of Climate -Resilient Fishermen Villages around 
rivers will be examined and considered for inclusion in the subsequent scheme. 
The Committee, appreciate the assurance given by the Department, and would 
further like to be apprised of the result of the said ev aluation of the PMMSY 
Scheme and their recommendation. 
 
ENHANCING THE CORPUS OF ACCIDENTAL LIFE INSURANCE FOR 
FISHERMEN 
(RECOMMENDATION PARA NO. 8) 
 
1.14 The Committee had observed/recommended: 
The Committee has been informed that the Department implements The Group 
Accident Insurance Scheme (GAIS) through National Fisheries Development 
Board (NFDB) under Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) since 
26th July, 2021, which provides life cover of Rs 5lac, 2.5lac and Rs. 25000 for 
fishermen against accidental death, accidental permanent/partial disability and 
accidental hospitalization respectively. Further the premium amount is shared 
between the centre and state in the ratio of 60:40 for general states, 90:10 for 
Himalayan and northeastern states and 100% by centre in case of Union 
Territories. 
The Committee are aware that most of the traditional fishermen/fishers belong 
to the socioeconomically disadvantaged strata lacking in financial stability and 
economic resources. Further, traditional fishers who venture into the sea for 
fishing activities are exposed to higher risks as fishing is one of the most 
dangerous occupations leading to many injuries and deaths annually due to 
harsh weather conditions and equipment failure. Any mishappening at sea 
leading to the loss of primary bread earner subjects the families of fishermen to 

 
10 
 
severe challenges to sustain their livelihood needs, and jeopardizes the future 
well-being of their families. Given the rising living costs and inflation, the current 
insurance cover would be insufficient to cover the basic survival needs, children 
education and debt repayments of fishermen who lose their lives. 
The Committee, therefore , recommend that the accidental Insurance cover 
under GAIS should be enhanced from Rs. 5 lac to at least Rs. 10 lac so that 
the families of the deceased fishermen are able to sustain their life with dignity 
and the financial security of their families is been taken care of. The Committee 
also observe that most of the times the fishermen families who claim the 
insurance cover are subjected to enormous paperwork and lengthy 
bureaucratic procedures and therefore, recommend that the proc edure for 
claiming insurance should be simplified and measures should be taken to 
ensure that the insurance amount is disbursed to the claimants promptly with 
least paperwork. 
 
1.15 In its Action Taken Reply, the Department has submitted: 
“The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana implemented by the 
Department has completed its schematic period on 31.03.2025 and currently 
under evaluation. Hence, increasing the accidental Insurance cover under 
GAIS from Rs. 5 lakh to Rs. 10 lakh shall be considered based on the outcomes 
of the evaluation. One online portal in this regard has been developed to submit 
the claim by the claimant/nominee/ legal heir with 120 days to process the claim 
settlement on first track basis.”

7. DEVELOPMENT OF SEAWEED CULTIVATION IN INDIA 
The Committee understands that Seaweeds are valued commercially for their 
cell wall polysaccharides such as agar, algin, carrageenan etc. and for the bioactive 
metabolites, manure and fodder and also have a variety of commercial applications in 
food, pharm aceutical, cosmetics, mining industry. Further, edible seaweeds 
(macroalgae) also have the potential to provide a rich and sustainable source of 
macronutrients and micronutrients to the human diet. Seaweed resources grow best 
in the tidal and inter -tidal waters along our peninsular coastline and the Andaman -
Nicobar and Lakshadweep Archipelagos. India is bestowed with more than 0.26 million 
tonnes wet harvestable biomass of seaweeds belonging to 700 species. Seaweed 
farming is a low-cost simple technology, which is one of the effective livelihood option 
for the marine fishers. 
The Committee has been informed that guidelines for allowing Import of live 
Seaweed have been issued recently which would enable domestic multiplication and 
ensure that farmers have access to quality seed stock which would bolster the 
development of seaweed enterprises in coastal states and Islands. 
Promotion of seaweed cultivation is one of the priority under Pradhan Mantri 
Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) and the country has enormous potential in 
seaweed cultivation which would improve the socioeconomic status of coastal/marine 
fishermen/farmers. The Committee, therefore, recommend that the Department may 
take proactive steps to promote seaweed cultivation in all the coastal states/Islands 
by providing financial, marketing and logistical support and ensure economic gains to 
the marginal marine fishermen  population along with protecting the marine 
ecosystems.  
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT:  
“Seaweed cultivation is one of the potential area for coastal regions. It is being 
cultivated in many of the Asian countries at commercial scale. Promotion of seaweed 
cultivation under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) is a major 
initiative by the Government of India to boost coastal aquaculture, enhance fisherfolk 
incomes, and support blue economy goals.  

 
22 
 
Among the coastal states, Tamil Nadu & Gujarat are the major producers. The 
Potential of seaweed production is around 9.7 million tonnes of seaweeds in 384 
identified potential sites in the country. Projects worth Rs.196.92 crore has been 
approved for seaweed cultivation through monoline, tube -net/raft method, R&D and 
training, including a Multipurpose Seaweed Park project in Tamil Nadu. Recently, 
ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute, Mand apam Regional Centre has 
also been notified by the Govern ment as Centre of Excellence (CoE) for Seaweed 
Promotion. 
Promotion of seaweed cultivation under PMMSY represents a transformative 
opportunity for India’s coastal communities. Targeted investments, technical support, 
and capacity-building initiatives have also been undertaken to promote a sustainable 
blue economy , economic empowerment, environmental conservation, and rural 
development.”

8. ENHANCING THE CORPUS OF ACCIDENTAL LIFE INSURANCE FOR 
FISHERMEN. 
 
The Committee has been informed that the Department implements The Group 
Accident Insurance Scheme (GAIS) through National Fisheries Development Board 
(NFDB) under Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) since 26 th July, 
2021, which provides life cover of Rs 5lac, 2.5lac and Rs. 25000 for fishermen against 
accidental death, accidental permanent/partial disability and accidental hospitalization 
respectively. Further the premium amount is shared between the centre and  state in 
the ratio of 60:40 for general states, 90:10 for Himalayan and north eastern states and 
100% by centre in case of Union Territories. 
The Committee are aware that most of the traditional fishermen/fishers belong to the 
socioeconomically disadvantaged strata lacking in financial stability and economic 
resources. Further, traditional fishers who venture into the sea for fishing activities are 
exposed to higher risks as fishing is one of the most dangerous occupations leading 
to many injuries and deaths annually due to harsh weather conditions and equipment 
failure. Any mishappening at sea leading to the loss of primary bread earner subjects 

 
23 
 
the families of fishermen to severe challenges to sustain their livelihood needs, and 
jeopardizes the future well -being of their families. Given the rising living costs and 
inflation, the current insurance cover would be insufficient to cover the basic sur vival 
needs, children education and debt repayments of fishermen who lose their lives. 
The Committee, therefore recommend that the accidental Insurance cover under GAIS 
should be enhanced from Rs. 5 lac to at least Rs. 10 lac so that the families of the 
deceased fishermen are able to sustain their life with dignity and the financial security 
of their families is been taken care of. The Committee also observe that most of the 
times the fishermen families who claim the insurance cover are subjected to enormous 
paperwork and lengthy bureaucratic procedures and therefore, recommend that the 
procedure for claiming insurance should be simplified and measures should be taken 
to ensure that the insurance amount is disbursed to the claimants promptly with least 
paperwork. 
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT:  
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana implemented by the Department has 
completed its schematic period on 31.03.2025 and currently under evaluation. Hence, 
increasing the accidental Insurance cover under GAIS from Rs. 5 lakh to Rs. 10 lakh 
shall be considered based on the outcomes of the evaluation. One online portal in this 
regard has been developed to submit the claim by the claimant/nominee/ legal heir 
with 120 days to process the claim settlement on first track basis.

Fisheries F. No. j-23011/3/2025-Fy(E-25457) Dated 25th June, 2025]

1. UNDERUTILIZATION OF ALLOCATED FUNDS AND INCREASING 
SHORTFALL 
 
The Committee in their 3 rd Report (DFG 2024 -25) at recommendation no. 1 
have observed that the revised procedure for release of central funds to States/UTs 
was introduced by the Department of Expenditure, MoF w.e.f. 31stJuly, 2021, and even 
after three years of its introduction, the desired results as envisaged by the 
Department, have not been achieved. The Committee, therefore, recommended that, 
the Department should make serious efforts and proactively liaise with its counterparts 
in the States/UTs and State Fisheries Departments to address this issue for positive 
results.  
Now, the Committee have been informed that to bring more efficiency in cash 
management at both Centre and States levels, an alternative fund flow mechanism for 
releasing central funds has been introduced on “Just -in-Time” basis under Centrally 
Sponsored Schemes (CSS) namely SNA -SPARSH from 1st June, 2024, wherein, 28 
schemes including Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) have been on 
boarded. Under the new system, 26 States have been on boarded, however, the pace 
of fund flow has been slow due to lack of understanding by the states to adhere to the 
compliances/guidelines of SNA-SPARSH, delay in contributing matching share by the 
State Governments and non -receipt of physical and financial progress (utilization 
certificates) on time from States/UTs and other stakeholders.  
The Committee are concerned that, the Department is unable to completely 
utilise the allocated budget and the shortfall of the Department has been increasing 
continuously. This underutilization of funds is also affecting the implementation and 
outcomes of the flagship scheme Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) 
and expenditure under the Scheduled Caste Sub Plan (SCSP) and Scheduled Tribes 
Sub Plan (STSP) which in turn is affecting the goals of uplifting the socio -economic 
conditions and general well being of the poor and traditional fishermen of the country. 
The Committee, therefore, recommend that the Department may explore the 

 
27 
 
possibility of devising an incentive scheme for State/UT governments, particularly to 
those States/UTs who promptly comply with the SNA -SPARSH guidelines, release 
their state matching share in time along with Utilisation Certificates and whose 
performance in implementing the schemes of the Department and spending under 
Scheduled Castes Sub Plan (SCSP), Scheduled Tribes Sub Plan (STSP) is 
substantial. The Committee  would like to be apprised of the steps taken by the 
Department and progress achieved in this regard. 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT:  
“The observation of the committee has been noted for necessary compliance. 
The Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance vide OM No.1(27)/PFMS/2020 
dated 13 th July 2023 has notified an alternative fund flow mechanism for releasing 
central funds to the State Governments on “ Just-in-Time” basis under Centrally 
Sponsored Schemes (CSS). This new system has been named as SNA-SPARSH 
wherein 28 schemes including PMMSY have been on boarded with effect from 1 st 
June, 2024. Under this new system, 28 States have been on-boarding on the SNA 
SPARSH platform. Lack of understanding by the states to adhere to the compliances 
of SNA -SPARSH, transition phase between SNA and SNA -SPARSH made the 
process slow for the States to adopt the new procedure and Non - compliance of the 
Guidelines in time by the States are few of the major point for slow expenditure. The 
Department has been working in close coordination with the States and these issues 
have been addressed from time to time. As such, better performance in the upcoming 
days is expected.” 
[Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Department of 
Fisheries F. No. j-23011/3/2025-Fy(E-25457) Dated 25th June, 2025]

28 
 
4. SCHEDULED CASTES SUB PLAN (SCSP) 
 The Committee in their 3 rd Report (DFG 2024 -25) at recommendation no 5, 
expressed serious concern at the declining trend of utilisaztion of funds under SCSP 
and recommended the Department to analyze the reasons for non -receipt of the 
proposals from the state Governments and initiat e suitable action including review of 
features, terms & conditions, eligibility criteria, etc and ensure the receipt of proposals 
from the state/ UT Governments for optimal utilization of the funds under SCSP.  
The Committee has been informed that the Government of India has highlighted the 
matter with the States/UTs having sizeable Schedule Caste beneficiaries in all the 
review meetings and they have been advised to ensure Mandatory earmarking of 
minimum 16.6% o f the budget of PMSSY for the benefits of scheduled caste 
beneficiaries. Further, States/UTs are advised to include SC/ST beneficiaries 
accordingly in their annual action plans and End Implementing Agencies I.e. Central 
Government entities including the Na tional Fisheries Development Board (NFDB) to 
include suitable interventions/activities for supporting SC population appropriately in 
their respective Annual Action Plan or Project Proposals.  
The Committee appreciates the efforts taken by the Department to ensure and 
encourage States/UTs to submit proposals under SCSP component of PMMSY , 
however, the Committee, observe that the actual expenditure of funds under SCSP 
component of PMMSY from the financial years 2022 -23 to 2024 -25 have been 
continuously decreasing. The Committee infers that decreasing actual expenditure of 
funds allocated for SCSP would mean that the efforts taken by the Department are not 
materializing in increasing actual expenditure under SCSP. The Committee, therefore 
recommend that the Department continue with their efforts so as to ensure maximum 
participation of Scheduled Castes population in the schemes implemented by the 
Department and reiterate their earlier recommendation  that the Department may 
devise a mechanism to incentivize /encourage States/UTs to send proposals under 
the SCSP so that the intended benefits of the scheme come to fruition. 
Reply of the Government:  
“The Department of Fisheries, Government of India, has consistently 
highlighted the matter in all review meetings with States/UTs having a sizeable 

 
29 
 
Scheduled Caste beneficiary population. The States/UTs also been advised to ensure 
that minimum 16.6% of the Schedule Caste beneficiaries are included for financial 
assistance in PMMSY project proposals while preparing the state annual action plan. 
Further, the measures taken up by the Department of Fisheries, Government of India 
in this regard include: (i) Mandatory earmarking of minimum 16.6% of the budget 
allocated under Schedule Cast Sub-Plan (SCSP) for the benefits of scheduled caste 
beneficiaries and advising States/UTs to include SC/ST beneficiaries accordingly in 
their annual action plans. Specific mention has been made in the annual 
administrative approval of the Scheme, in accordance with the Ministry of Finance's 
instructions, that the funds earma rked for Scheduled Caste beneficiaries are to be 
utilized exclusively for their development (ii) Requesting the End Implementing 
Agencies i.e. Central Government entities including the National Fisheries 
Development Board (NFDB) to include suitable interve ntions/activities for supporting 
SC population appropriately in their respective Annual Action Plan or Project 
Proposals. Similarly, State Governments and Union Territories are regularly requested 
to make specific allocations for Scheduled Castes in their Annual Action Plans, self-
contained proposals, and Detailed Project Reports (DPRs), based on the percentage 
of the SC population within their jurisdiction.” 
[Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Department of 
Fisheries F. No. j-23011/3/2025-Fy(E-25457) Dated 25th June, 2025]

9. MATSYA SEVA KENDRA (MSK) 
 The Committee has been informed that Matsya Seva Kendra (MSKs) are 
integral components of the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) 
established to enhance the fisheries sector in India. They function as a One -Stop 
Solution Centers offering a range o f services to fishers and fish farmers, including 
water, soil, and microbial analysis, disease testing, and capacity -building programs 
along with Extension and Support Services to disseminate modern aquaculture 

 
30 
 
practices, technological advancements, and best practices available in fisheries 
management. Further, establishment of Matsya Seva Kendra (MSK) under PMMSY 
are based on proposals submitted by the concerned States/UTs. 
The Committee understand that MSK can play an important role in the overall 
development of the fisheries sector by increasing awareness amongst fishermen 
about the modern aquaculture practices, technological interventions and also 
strengthening capacity bu ilding. The Committee, therefore recommend that the 
Department should take effective measures and ensure that Matsya Seva Kendra are 
established in every district of the country which has a sizeable population engaged in 
fisheries for their livelihood and economic wellbeing. The Department should actively 
pursue with States/UTs and incentivize them for establishing Matsya Seva Kendra on 
priority basis. 
Reply of the Government:  
“Establishing Matsya Seva Kendras  (MSKs) is an important initiative aimed at 
strengthening the fisheries sector, especially under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya 
Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) in India. These Kendras function as single-window service 
centers to support fishers, fish farmers, entreprene urs, and other stakeholders in 
fisheries and aquaculture. Setting up Matsya Seva Kendras is a pivotal step in making 
India’s fisheries sector more organized, empowered, and sustainable. These centers 
can greatly improve fishers' livelihoods by acting as kn owledge and resource hubs, 
ensuring the holistic growth of the Blue Economy. Under PMMSY 102 numbers of 
Matsya Seva Kendras has been approved. All the States/UTs are requested in various 
review meeting to promote such Extension and support services to act as a last-mile 
delivery mechanism for fishers and fishermen in the country.”  
[Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Department of 
Fisheries F. No. j-23011/3/2025-Fy(E-25457) Dated 25th June, 2025]

OVERVIEW OF DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND 
FARMERS WELFARE 
 
 
Mandate 
 
The Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) serves as a key 
Department in strengthening India’s agricultural sector by boosting productivity, 
ensuring food security, and improving the livelihoods of farmers. Its mandate 
focuses on promoting sustainable agricultural development through modern 
farming techniques and resource-efficient practices. A core objective of the 
Department is to enhance crop productivity by implementing schemes that 
improve soil health, expand irrigation coverage, and increase overall farm 
efficiency. DA&FW is also responsible for framing agricultural policies, including 
crop pricing mechanisms, promotion of organic and natural farming, and the 
development of a unified national agricultural market to safeguard farmers’ 
interests. Through flagship initiatives such as Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman 
Nidhi (PM-KISAN), the Department provides direct income support to small and 
marginal farmers, enabling them to access essential agricultural inputs and 
maintain financial stability.  Additionally, the Department promotes research in 
areas such as advanced farming practices, pest management, and crop 
diversification to encourage sustainable agriculture. It works closely with State 
Governments to implement Central Sector Schemes effectively, monitor 
agricultural data, and strengthen local agricultural initiatives across the country. 
 

2  
1.2  Two new Schemes namely Bharat-VISTAAR and Support for High 
Value Agriculture have been announced in the Union Budget (2026-27). 
Bharat-VISTAAR is a new AI-powered, multilingual digital platform launched to 
provide farmers with real-time advisories, weather updates, market prices, 
scheme details and crop support in a single gateway, improving farm decisions 
and productivity. The Bharat VISTAAR tool integrates data from multiple sources 
like weather, APMC prices, pest alerts and scientific guidance to offer 
personalised support in local languages, including voice access for basic 
phones. The newly launched Scheme, Support for High Value Agriculture will 
focus on enhancing cultivation and processing of crops such as cashew, cocoa, 
sandalwood and other niche, high-return crops with the objective of increasing 
income by strengthening existing post harvesting mechanisms, value chains and 
boosting export competitiveness of high-value produce.

Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK)  
1.23 Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) are pivotal agricultural extension centers 
established to enhance the productivity and sustainability of agriculture. They 
were initiated to serve as a bridge between agricultural research and the farming 
community. KVKs focus on assessing and demonstrating location-specific 
agricultural technologies tailored to local conditions. This involves conducting on-
farm testing (OFT) and frontline demonstrations (FLD) to validate these 
technologies in real-world settings. They aim to develop the skills and knowledge 
of farmers through various training programs, workshops, and educational 
initiatives. This includes both short-term and long-term training courses designed 
for different target groups, including women and youth. KVKs provide farm 
advisory services using information and communication technology (ICT) to 
disseminate knowledge about modern agricultural practices, pest management, 
and crop production techniques. KVKs organize training sessions for farmers, 
extension personnel, and other stakeholders to update their knowledge about 
agricultural innovations. They conduct demonstrations to showcase the potential 
of various crops and farming techniques, helping farmers understand the 

19  
practical applications of research findings. Acting as knowledge hubs, KVKs 
compile and share valuable resources related to agricultural technologies, 
including seeds, planting materials, and bio-agents.

1.25 The Department was asked to furnish as to which budgetary provisions 
have been made in Union Budget 2026–27 to enhance the financial sustainability 
and claim-settlement capacity of AIC under schemes like Pradhan Mantri Fasal 
Bima Yojana (PMFBY). In its reply, the Department has submitted: 
 
“There is no budgetary provision in Union Budget 2026-27 to enhance the financial 
sustainability and claim settlement capacity of AIC under schemes like PMFBY.  
However, in the Union Budget 2026-27, the Government has made continuity and 
targeted provisioning for crop insurance, which underpins the financial sustainability 
and claim handling capacity of implementing agencies such as the Agriculture 
Insurance Company of India (AIC) under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana 
(PMFBY). Some of the provisions are: 
Dedicated Budget Allocation for Crop Insurance: 
 The Budget continues to allocate substantial funds for the PMFBY under the 
Department of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, with an estimated ₹12,200 crore 
earmarked for the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana in 2026-27. This continued 
funding ensures that the financial underpinnings required for risk coverage and 
consequential claims disbursement remain in place for the scheme’s operations 
throughout the year.  
 Support for Innovation and Technology: A Fund for Innovation and Adoption of 
Technology (FIAT) has been provided with a modest yet positive allocation (₹200 
crore) to support adoption of new technologies relevant to agriculture, including 
risk assessment and monitoring tools. This kind of technology funding contributes 
toward improving crop loss estimation and expediting claim settlement 
processes, which are critical to governance efficiency and insurer cash-flows.  
 Overall Agriculture Support Framework: While the budget primarily focuses on 
technology, diversification, and farmer advisory services (e.g., the Bharat-
VISTAAR AI platform), these measures strengthen the broader ecosystem within 
which crop insurance operates by reducing exposure to risk and improving data 
quality for yield forecasting and claim validation.  
 Sustaining Risk Mitigation Capacity: Although the Budget did not substantially 
increase the PMFBY outlay compared to previous years, the continuity of finance 
for PMFBY, combined with technology-led interventions and a large overall 

21  
agricultural allocation (₹1.63 lakh crore), provides a stable fiscal framework 
enabling schemes like PMFBY to function without disruption, thereby supporting 
AIC’s capacity to maintain business continuity.   
 In summary, the Budget 2026-27 maintains core funding for PMFBY, supports 
technological enhancements via FIAT and allied digital tools, and reinforces the 
overall agricultural budgetary ecosystem. These combined provisions help 
sustain the financial base of crop insurance delivery and improve the claim 
settlement capacity of agencies such as AIC — especially critical for coverage 
continuity and farmer trust.” 
        
 
1.26 On being asked to furnish details as to in what ways does the Budget  
2026–27 address issues of delayed claim settlements by AIC, especially in 
climate-vulnerable regions, the Department has submitted: 
 “The budget addresses the issue of delayed claims settlement in the following ways: 
 
 The Budget recognises the importance of digital and AI-driven systems in 
agriculture. It supports technology frameworks such as the Fund for Innovation and 
Adoption of Technology (FIAT) for PMFBY and the Bharat-VISTAAR AI platform, 
which are intended to improve data collection, real-time crop loss assessment, and 
decision support.  
 These technological enhancements can reduce the time taken for field loss 
assessment and claims verification, cutting the long settlement lags reported in 
climate-impacted areas. Accurate, automated and remote yield assessment tools 
(innovation enabled through FIAT funding) help expedite claims processing in 
areas where traditional manual assessments are slow, inconsistent, or prone to 
dispute.  
 With the introduction of an Output-Outcome Monitoring Framework (OOMF) to 
track scheme performance, there is an institutional push toward strengthened 
monitoring of scheme delivery including key indicators like claim disbursement 
timelines. This improved transparency and performance measurement can 
indirectly pressure implementing agencies, including insurance companies, to 
adhere to operational timelines of claim settlements.” 
 
1.27 On being asked as to how the AIC is expected to leverage digital 

22  
technologies and AI-based assessment tools, as emphasized in Budget 2026–
27, for faster and more accurate crop loss estimation, the Department has 
submitted: 
“It is submitted that under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), digital 
technologies and remote sensing–based assessment tools are already being 
operationalized for crop loss estimation, in line with the emphasis in Union Budget 
2026–27 on leveraging digital technologies and AI-based assessment tools for faster 
and more accurate crop loss estimation. 
Satellite-derived indices such as Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) are 
used for monitoring crop health and vegetation stress, while Land Surface Water 
Index (LSWI) and similar spectral indicators are employed for identification of flood 
and waterlogging–affected areas. 
 Primarily, data from the Sentinel satellite series (Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-
3) are utilized for agricultural analysis. With spatial resolutions of 10–20 metres and 
revisit cycles of about 5 days for Sentinel-2 and 12 days for Sentinel-1, crops are 
monitored consistently throughout the crop cycle, from sowing to harvest, enabling 
timely detection of stress and damage. 
Further, these multi-temporal satellite indicators are integrated with weather 
parameters and historical yield data through Artificial Intelligence and Machine 
Learning (AI/ML) models to objectively classify affected areas and quantify crop 
damage. Such data-driven models support faster turnaround time and improved 
accuracy in loss assessment, particularly during large-scale calamities such as 
droughts and floods, thereby reducing subjectivity associated with manual 
assessments. 
The generated remote sensing outputs are also expected to play a significant role in 
supporting dispute-resolution mechanisms across different forums in future, by 
providing objective and time-stamped evidence of crop conditions. Additionally, the 
study facilitates assessment of cost–benefit aspects of satellite-based monitoring in 
comparison with drone-based approaches. 
AIC is also in discussions with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) to utilize 
various datasets available in the public domain. These datasets will be accessed via 
the IMD API and integrated into the inhouse developed GCMS platform of the 
Company  for various risk management activities.”

agriculture from pilot projects to mainstream policy, with AIC leading in delivering financial

“High-value agriculture strategy focuses on shifting from low-value staple crops to 
high-return activities to increase farmer incomes and generate rural employment.

markets, which helps farmers diversify income and reduce dependence on a single 
crop, while also creating more jobs across the value chain.

1.50 On being asked to state as to how will the Department ensure that lack of 
post-harvest management facilities does not negate the potential profitability of 
High Value for Agriculture (HVA) in view of the fact that the perishability of high-

submitted: 
 
“The Department recognizes that perishability and quality sensitivity of high-value 
agricultural commodities (horticulture, floriculture, plantation crops, etc.) require 
strong post-harvest infrastructure to prevent losses and distress sales. To ensure that 
infrastructure gaps do not undermine the profitability of High-Value Agriculture (HVA), 
a multi-pronged strategy is being implemented as detailed below: 
 
1. Cluster-Based Infrastructure Development: Promotion of HVA through cluster-
based planning, ensuring production areas are supported with pack-houses, 
cold storage, grading/sorting units, ripening chambers and primary processing 
facilities. 
2. Financial Support for Cold Chain and Processing Infrastructure: Capital 
investment support under schemes such as MIDH and Agriculture Infrastructure 
Fund (AIF) for cold storages, integrated pack-houses, reefer vans, controlled 

45  
atmosphere units and value-addition facilities, along with interest subvention and 
credit guarantee mechanisms. 
3. Farm-Gate and FPO-Led Aggregation Models: Strengthening Farmer Producer 
Organizations (FPOs) to aggregate produce, undertake primary grading and 
improve market linkages. 
4. Promotion of Primary Processing at Source: Establishment of decentralized 
small-scale processing units including drying, dehydration and minimal 
processing to extend shelf life. 
5. Strengthening Market Linkages and Logistics: Improved logistics planning, 
integration with electronic trading platforms and linkage with institutional buyers 
and exporters. 
6. Capacity Building and Standardization: Training farmers and FPOs in scientific 
post-harvest handling, grading, packaging and quality compliance. 
7. Convergence and Public–Private Participation: Convergence with other 
schemes and facilitation of private investment through credit facilitation and 
viability gap support.

institutional strengthening, credit facilitation and capacity building, the 
Department aims to minimize post-harvest losses, stabilize prices and safeguard 
the profitability of High-Value Agriculture across regions.”

2.31 On being asked to state as to whether the Department has constituted any 
Task Force or Study Group to monitor the premiums being paid by the Farmers 
under PMFBY and any plans to decrease these premiums and if any comparative 
study made by the Department of premiums paid on account of Crop Insurance 
under PMFBY with other existing Crop Insurance Schemes in the world has been 
done, the Department has submitted : 
“During implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) after 
revamping it w.e.f kharif 2020 seasons,  following major concerns were expressed by 
most of the implementing States (i) due to low underwriting capacity of the insurance 
companies, few companies are participating in bidding process (ii) there is prevalence 
of high premium rates  and (iii)  low claim ratio etc.  To sort out these issues/concerns 
of the States, Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare has constituted a Working 
Group on 13th September, 2021 under the Chairmanship of CEO, PMFBY & JS 
(Credit).  The Working Group examined the alternative risk mitigation mechanisms to 
rationalise the premium pricing, enhancing underwriting capacity and challenges faced 
in implementation of the scheme.  During its deliberations, the Group has also 
constituted 2 sub-committees namely, (i) Sub-Committee on Actuarial Aspects under 
the Chairmanship of Joint Secretary (Insurance), Deptt. of Financial Services and (ii) 
Sub-Committee on Yield Estimation using Technology under the Chairmanship of Dr. 
KR Manjunath, Group Director, ISRO.   

71  
 
 Based on the recommendations of the Working Group, the scheme has been 
revised with effect from Kharif 2023 season, wherein alternative risk sharing models 
namely, Cup & Cap Model  (80 : 110), Cup & Cap Model  (60 : 130), profit and loss 
sharing models as  suggested by the Group have been adopted and flexibility has been 
given to the States and UTs to choose model as per their needs and availability of 
financial/budgetary allocations.   Under 80  : 110 model, if claims are below 80% of total 
premium then a portion of the premium is returned to the State Government by the 
insurance company.  On the other hand if claims are above 110% of the premium then 
the State Government pays these claims above 110% of premium.   Central 
Government has no sharing in surplus and additional claims over 110% of premium 
under this model.  However, in case of 60 : 130 model, Central Government shares 
surpluses with State Government, if claims are below 60% of total premium and shares 
claims in case of claims above 130% of premium.  In the current tender cycle for 2023-
2025, 4 inactive insurers have started participating.  Additionally 2 more insurers have 
been empanelled and therefore number of active insurers have increased from 11 in 
2020 tendering cycle to 15 in 2023-25 tender cycle. 
 
Further, technology based yield estimation is also being implemented from Kharif 2023 
season.   
 Due to these improvements based on various committees, reports;  a large 
participation of Insurance companies and high level of competition in bidding has been 
witnessed in 2023-25  tender cycle, which has reduced the premium rates to 10.2% in 
2024-25  as compared to 16.7% in 2020-21. 
 An impact assessment study of the scheme has also been conducted through an 
independent agency.”

Observations/Recommendations 
 
ANALYSIS OF DEMANDS FOR GRANTS- DEMAND NO.1 
 
ALLOCATION OF BUDGETARY RESURCES AND THEIR UTILIZATION 
 
 
1. The Committee note that the Department of Agriculture and Farmers 
Welfare has been allocated Rs. 130561.39 Crore for 2026-27 at BE stage 
whereas the Actual expenditure on Agriculture & Farmers Welfare in 2024-
25 was Rs 1,29,933.47 crore which means a hike of only around Rs 627.91 
crore or simply put a 0.5% nominal growth, over a period of two years and 
that too without factoring the rate of inflation. The actual utilization of funds 
for 2025-26 as on 31.01.2026 is Rs. 79,233.42 Crore w.r.t. RE stands at  
64.37% which clearly indicates that the Department needs to strive hard to 
fully utilize the funds in the remaining period of two months(approx.) of the 
current FY 2025-26. The Committee also note that RE of the Department for 

85  
FY 2025-26 is Rs.123,089.30 Crore which is Rs.4200.86 Crore less than its 
BE of Rs.127,290.16 Crore.  
The Committee are of the view that in case the Department is not able 
to spend the remaining funds in the last two months of FY 2025-26, there 
are high chances of not getting the enhanced allocations as sought by the 
Department, as the Ministry of Finance might take a stand that as 
surrendering of funds was done in the past, demand for allocating the 
entire amount sought by the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 
may not be acceded to.  The Committee recommend that the Department 
may expend funds in an equitable, time-bound manner as prescribed by 
Department of Expenditure guidelines for achievement of outcome and 
output targets under various Schemes, programmes, Missions etc.  
 
The Committee recommend the Department to use real-time digital 
dashboards having Artificial Intelligence(AI) features and quarterly 
variance reviews on a regular basis  which would provide the Department 
with a real time digital oversight thereby ensuring fiscal discipline, 
transparency, and efficient delivery of public services. The Department 
must also look into issues which are pending for more than six months and 
address them which are hampering the entire spending of the allocated 

86  
amounts. The Department also needs to spruce up their Financial 
Management system as year after year the prescribed limits of Quarter wise 
spending laid down by Department of Expenditure are not being adhered 
to. The processes need to be streamlined & guidelines be amended 
accordingly, if required, to optimize utilization of funds.  
NEED FOR ENHANCEMENT OF BUDGETARY ALLOCATION TO 
DEPARTMENT 
 
2. The Committee observe that the proportion of budgetary allocation 
made in favour of the Department in terms of the percentage of the total 
Central outlay for the years 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, 2025-26 and 2026-27 
stood at 3.14%, 2.57%,2.54%,2.51% and 2.44% respectively. This shows 
continuous decline in the allocations to the Department as proportion of 
Central Plan outlay. 
The Committee note that Agriculture and allied activities account for 
46.1 % of the country’s workforce but contribute only one-fifth of India’s 
national income at current prices. This disparity highlights the Agriculture 
sector's vulnerability and the urgent need for increased public investment. 
Agriculture remains the backbone of India’s growth trajectory given the fact 
that the sector   employs a large share of workforce. The Committee feel 
that investment in agriculture has a higher multiplier effect on poverty 
reduction than investment in many other sectors. Strengthening 

87  
agricultural performance is therefore important for inclusive growth, 
economic stability and ensuring food security.  
The Committee recommend that the budgetary allocation to the 
Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) is a strategic 
investment in the nation's economic sovereignty & not just a welfare 
measure and more importantly, to complement and supplement the 
overarching goal of the Union government in doubling farmers' income 
effectively. Enhanced budgetary allocation will enable the Department to 
potently counter the challenges of Climate Change, fragmented 
landholdings, increasing disruptions in global supply chains, market 
volatility and so on as these require a swift and robust financial response. 
Enhanced budgetary allocations to the Department will facilitate in its 
transition from subsistence farming to sustainable agri-business, thereby 
ensuring food security for the nation and prosperity for the Annadata (food 
provider). 
 
NEED TO ENHANCE RATE OF GROWTH IN CAPITAL FORMATION IN 
AGRICULTURE 
 
3. The Committee note that Agriculture is the backbone of our economy 
& dependence on Nature enhances the risk quotient of our Agriculture and 
this is precisely where high growth rate of Capital formation in agriculture 

88  
can effectively mitigate the risks arising due to natural calamities.  It is a 
proven fact that the growth of capital formation is a vital prerequisite for 
agricultural development.  Capital Formation in Agriculture refers to 
investment in-(i) creating physical assets such as infrastructure (ii) 
upgradation and honing of skills of human resources; and (iii) institutional 
capacity to boost productivity.  
Sustained growth in agricultural output and farmer incomes depends 
mainly on higher capital formation in agriculture. The rate of growth in 
Capital Formation in Agriculture is essential to enhance productivity as the 
most significant impact of increase in capital formation is the increase in 
yield per hectare. Growth in agricultural capital creates demand for 
industrial goods such as fertilizers, pesticides and so on. Increased 
agricultural output supplies raw materials to industries such as textiles and 
food processing. Strong infrastructure enables farmers in getting higher 
price realization for their agricultural produce. Thus, capital formation in 
agriculture acts as an engine for overall industrial growth too. 
The growth rate in Capital Formation (at current prices) in Agriculture 
and Allied Sector during the year 2019-20 was 5.1% which rose to 22.8% 
during the period 2020-21, then fell down to 15.5% in the year 2021-22, 
increased marginally during 2022-23 to 16.1% and then fell significantly to 

89  
9.6% during the period 2023-24. 
The Committee also note that the budget outlay for Agriculture & 
Farmers Welfare was Rs.1,24,000 Crore in 2022-23 whereas the total Budget 
outlay of the Union Government was Rs.39,44,908.6 Crore for the same 
period. Similarly, the budgetary allocation to Agriculture in 2026-27 BE is 
Rs. 130,561.38 Crore whereas the total budget outlay of the Union 
Government is Rs.53,47,315 Crore. Simply put, from 2022-23 to 2026-27, 
there is an increase of Rs.6561.38 Crore in Budgetary allocation for 
Agriculture and Farmers Welfare whereas the Total Budget outlay of the 
Union Government increased by Rs 14,02,406.34 Crore during the same 
period which indicates that the budgetary allocation for Agriculture did not 
get an increase in the same proportion. The Actual Expenditure in total 
Scheme Budget (Central Sector + Centrally Sponsored Schemes) of 
Agriculture in 2020-21 was Rs.1,08,090.13 Crore, out of which the  Actual 
expenditure incurred on PM-KISAN and Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima 
Yojana(PMFBY) was Rs.75151.38 Crore, which translates into Actual 
Expenditure of Rs.32938.75 Crore on other heads including creation of 
Capital Assets. This meant that around 69.53% of total Scheme Budget of 
Agriculture was spent on payment to farmers and Insurance companies 
during the period 2020-21. Similarly, the Actual Expenditure in Total 

90  
Scheme Budget (Central Sector+ Centrally Sponsored Schemes) of 
Agriculture in 2024-25 was Rs.128763.55 Crore, out of which the  Actual 
expenditure incurred on PM-KISAN and PMFBY was Rs.80594.66 Crore, 
which results into Actual Expenditure of Rs.48168.89 Crore on other heads 
including creation of Capital Assets. This meant that around 62.59% of total 
Scheme Budget of Agriculture was spent on payment to farmers and 
Insurance companies during the period 2024-25. Simply put, majority of the 
expenditure of total Scheme Budget of Agriculture goes on payments being 
made to  Farmers and Insurance companies, leaving less for investment  in 
Capital Assets and modernization of Agriculture including creating 
resilience against Climate Change.  
 The Committee recommend the Government to enhance investments 
significantly in Capital, human and institutional assets in agriculture to 
ensure that the rate of Capital Formation in Agriculture and Allied Sector 
does not come below 15% as the growth in rate of capital formation in 
agriculture is not merely an economic metric but a strategic imperative to 
ensure food security, economic stability and stimulate industrial growth.  
   
IMPORTANCE OF FARM LABOURER AND THE NEED FOR THEIR 
INCLUSION IN THE MANDATE OF DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE 
AND FARMERS WELFARE  

91  
 
4. The Committee are of the view that Farm Labourers are an important 
component of the Agricultural ecosystem in the country. Farm Labourers 
face unique & diverse challenges which are totally different than faced by 
any other class of Labourers including industrial labourers. In the current 
welfare measures being implemented by the Ministry right focus is being 
accorded for farmer welfare, but the labour which provides the necessary 
workforce in the agriculture fields is unable to reap the benefit as they do 
not own the land which they till. The Committee feel that the Department of 
Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) should make concerted efforts for 
identifying the unique challenges being faced by the labourers working on 
the farms. The Committee further note that while the   Ministry of Labour is 
the nodal Ministry to implement the welfare schemes for the labour class 
in the country, however farm labour being a distinct category and are 
different from industrial labour. As such, the agriculture labour are not 
identified as workmen/industrial labour and they are unable to reap the 
benefits being accorded to industrial labourers viz. Medical Care, Insurance 
and social Security. In this backdrop the Committee recommend that the 
Ministry Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) should consider to widen 
the ambit of component of Farmer Welfare and should include the welfare 

92  
of Farm Labourers within its scope. The Committee also recommend that 
the Ministry needs to identify programmes, schemes, missions etc for their 
inclusion in specific social security schemes such as pension funds, 
Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana, and maternity benefits tailored 
specifically for agricultural labourers. 
 
SCHEDULED CASTES SUB PLAN(SCSP) 
 
5. The Committee are of the considered view that Scheduled Castes Sub 
Plan (SCSP), is an important budgetary mechanism designed to uplift the 
Scheduled Castes (SC). The Committee feel that the Department should 
more proactively pursue the release of funds under the SCSP with State 
Governments and implementing agencies.  Concerted efforts should be 
made in coordination with State Governments to chalk out strategies to 
deal with problems which hitherto exist, after taking into account, the 
ground realities which may relate to Terms & conditions, eligibility criteria 
etc. The Committee strongly feel that funds utilization under Scheduled 
Castes Sub Plan needs to be enhanced and procedural difficulties, if any, 
existing in regard to the same, may be addressed at the earliest. The 
Committee accordingly recommend that : 
(i) Terms and conditions(T&C) of the scheme may be regularly 

93  
revisited to check their alignment with existing ground realities 
and suitable amendments be made after consulting all 
stakeholders; 
(ii) Mandatory social audits of SCSP  by third party be done to 
impart transparency and accountability in the existing system; 
(iii) ensure compliance that funds allocated under SCSP remain 
non- divertible and are used exclusively for SCSP initiatives 
only;  
(iv) Need to shift plan to output-outcome budgeting; and 
(v) wide publicity in local dialects may be given in digital platforms, 
radio, tv, mobiles(KVK farmer /extension Whatsapp groups 
/SMS) detailing benefits of the Scheme.
